correctness.rationale: For all n>=2, every directed cycle in K2n is a four-cycle, equivalent to simultaneous occurrence of 01 and 10 columns. Two three-letter product alphabets with two-letter intersection give the exact coefficient by inclusion-exclusion. The zero classification follows by parity and 3-adic versus 2-adic prime factors; all quantifiers and n=1 boundary are explicit. Walsh diagonalization proves rank 4^n/2, min positive singular value 2 by a two-mixed-column witness, max 2*3^n-2^n at the trivial frequency, and the reversal-invariant projection. Exact-integer FWHT checked all frequencies for n=2..7, while direct directed-cycle search separately checked n=2..5. Tests corroborate but do not replace the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The complete 2n-coordinate signed Walsh coefficient formula, exact zero support, rank, sharp nonzero spectral gap and reversal-invariant recovery space were not implied by the inspected source statements. Cameron et al. identify 2xn lonesum matrices and unweighted counts; Kamano et al. enumerate by a single total-entry weight; West studies dependent-edge counts; Stanley proves chromatic evaluation. These are mathematically different functions/invariants. The proof gives a genuine multivariate refinement and checks all characters rather than just the trivial or all-one character. Limited-index risk remains for an unlocated equivalent entrywise signed-weight enumerator.
residual_risks: A non-indexed or inadequately searchable per-entry signed-weight lonesum polynomial might imply the formula.
Summary-only indexed claims were not treated as full-text exclusions; their stated objects and conclusions differ.
Priority is assessed only against accessible cited literature and actual indexed semantic searches, not all historical publications.

value.rationale: The natural binary incidence family of all acyclic orientations of K2n corresponds to the classical lonesum matrices, yet its full edge-wise Walsh convolution has a distinct inverse problem. This all-width theorem determines exactly which data cannot be recovered (global reversal odd modes), rules out every additional cancellation, gives full signed multipliers with multiplicities and the exact exponential stability constant, and constructs a norm-one projection onto all recoverable data. This is more informative than a textbook total count or a particular finite numerical experiment; the width is arbitrary and the full mode classification matters for harmonic inverse reconstruction.
